story.head: Bring a pillow
paras: The Blues won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-4 in Detroit on Oct 31. The Blues are winless in three (0-2-1), and the Red Wings are on a three-game losing streak. Going in, the Wings are last in the Atlantic (tied for 21st in the NHL) and the Blues seventh in the Central (25th).

The Red Wings have played better than their record (.472) says: their chances are worth about .580, and their finishing has held them back. So have the Blues (.471 on chances worth .553), where their finishing has held them back.

The Red Wings block more shots than almost anyone (2nd), leave the shooting to their forwards (3rd lowest) and draw more penalties than they take (4th). As for the Blues, they keep things calm after the whistle (lowest) and rarely get pinned in their own end (3rd). They also have struggled on the power play (31st), so the Red Wings’ power play bites, but their doesn’t. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one.

Alex DeBrincat (7 G / 9 A / 16 P in 18 GP) leads the Red Wings in scoring, and Viktor Arvidsson (8 G / 7 A / 15 P in 18 GP) has a team-high eight goals. For the Blues, Philip Broberg (4 G / 9 A / 13 P in 17 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Jimmy Snuggerud (9 G / 3 A / 12 P in 17 GP) has a team-high nine goals.
Daniil Tarasov (2-3-2 / .919 SV% in 6 GS) has been terrific for Detroit and will likely start. Joel Hofer (6-5-1 / .919 SV% in 12 GS) has been outstanding for St. Louis and will likely start.
